exposure: Post-bariatric surgery women with SUD during pregnancy vs. without SUD
cohort: 1849 adult women (18-45 years old) who underwent bariatric surgery between 1996 and 2016 and gave birth after surgery between 1996 and 2018
finding: Post-bariatric surgery women who had substance use disorders (SUD) during pregnancy experienced significantly more pregnancy and birth complications, including preterm birth, low birth weight, cesarean delivery, and neonatal intensive care unit admission, compared to those without SUD, despite a lower risk of macrosomia.
mod_finding: Women with SUD during pregnancy had a significantly higher risk of Cesarean delivery (OR = 9.71, p < 0.01, 95% CI: 2.69-35.05) compared to women without SUD.
